newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee surges, London seen opening down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee surges, London seen opening down.

text.p: Indonesian Robusta coffee prices surged on Monday in step with gains in London as buyers scoured villages for beans while farmers held back sales in anticipation of higher values, traders said.

Grade four Robusta was quoted at 4,300-4,350 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, compared with 3,450 rupiah a week ago. The export price was quoted at $1,800-$1,850/tonne FOB Lampung, against $1,500 last Monday.
The traders said London's benchmark July futures contract was expected to open $10-$20 lower later on Monday, but they expected prices to move upwards through the rest of the day.

"It's just crazy," one trader said, commenting on how prices have soared amid a scorching speculative rally in both the New York and London markets on a mix of low stocks, tight Latin American supply and worries of another frost in Brazil.

"Buyers are venturing into villages to look for beans, instead of waiting for them to come into town," one trader said. "This is because farmers are beginning to hold back as they expect prices to improve further."
Another trader said he expected the bullish sentiment on coffee to be sustained through the week.
